subject: Architecture
title: Minimalism: The Architecture of Nothing
description: A quick win: understand Minimalism: The Architecture of Nothing.

hook.text: Minimalist architecture strips away everything until only light, space, and surface remain.

buildup.text: John Pawson and Tadao Ando create spaces so bare that a shadow becomes the main feature.

discovery.text: Ando's concrete walls have no paint, no plaster — just the raw surface with tiny holes from formwork.

twist.text: Minimalist homes are expensive to build. Perfection in nothing requires obsessive attention to detail.

climax.text: Apple stores worldwide use minimalist architecture — clean lines, glass, and emptiness as luxury.

punchline.text: Nothing is harder to build than nothing.

quiz.question: Why are minimalist buildings paradoxically expensive?
options: Perfection in simplicity demands obsessive attention to detail
Building codes require extra structural reinforcement
